findings.problem: Source57 Statement(b) indexes Slater family by ordered tuples even though its definition, proof and62 consumers use n-element subsets.

paragraphs:
(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\rho_i(k)}$;

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\sigma(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\sigma(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

1.3 [Orthonormality of the Slater family] For subsets $J,K$ with $|J|=|K|=n$ put $A_{ab}:=\langle e_{j_a},e_{k_b}\rangle=\delta_{j_a,k_b}$. By [F1], $\langle e_J^\wedge,e_K^\wedge\rangle=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma,\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)\prod_{l=1}^n A_{\sigma(l),\pi(l)}$. For each fixed $\pi$ substitute $\sigma=\omega\pi$ and reindex the product by $t=\pi(l)$. Then $\prod_l A_{\sigma(l),\pi(l)}=\prod_t A_{\omega(t),t}$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\omega)$, so the sum over $\pi$ contributes $n!$ and the remaining sum is $\det(A)$ by [F3]. For $J=K$, $A=I_n$ and this is $1$; for $J\ne K$, some $j_a$ is absent from $K$, giving a zero row and determinant $0$. Thus the Slater family is orthonormal. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

[F3] **Product basis and occupation bases.** The elementary tensors $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ over all multi-indices form an orthonormal basis of $K^{\otimes N}$; the Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_N})$ over $N$-element subsets $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(N)}$ with $e_J^\wedge$ zero-free for distinct indices and vanishing on repeated indices; the vectors $m_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$ over $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ form an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(N)}$, and $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$, $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F4] **Configuration counts.** The map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection from $N$-element subsets onto $\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$, the sector dimensions are $\binom dN$ and $\binom{N+d-1}{N}$, and for $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b)).

2.1 [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.1 [Fermionic configuration sum] The two-element subsets of $\{1,2,3\}$ are $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$ with energies $0+\varepsilon=\varepsilon$, $0+2\varepsilon=2\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon+2\varepsilon=3\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_J=e^{-\beta\lambda_J}/Z_{\mathrm F}$, and the occupation means are $\sum_Jq_J\mathbf 1_J(j)$ by [L2], giving the three displayed formulas. The total occupation is $\sum_Jq_J\cdot2=2$ because every configuration has two occupied modes, and the smallest energy is that of $\{1,2\}$, namely $\varepsilon$, by [L1] clause (c). This proves (a). [L1, L2, algebra]

findings.problem: Lemma Statement(d) passes a two-argument expression to the one-argument partial trace and conjugates the resulting H-endomorphism by the full-space parenthesisation map J_n. J_n has incompatible source/target. Proof3.1 obtains the correctly typed partial trace of J_n rho-tilde J_n^-1, then identifies gamma as its conjugate. Correct reduced operator is partial trace itself on H.

paragraphs:
(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$;

3.1 [Reduction to one slot, the trace law and the reduced operator] Fix $i$ and $\pi$ with $\pi(1)=i$; by steps 1.3 and 2.1 and [F7], $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*)=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)$, where the middle equality is cyclicity and the last uses $U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi=\widetilde\rho$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)=n\operatorname{tr}((O\otimes I)J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1})=n\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1})O)$ by [F7], [F5] and the explicit form of $A_1$ in step 1.2; with the definition of $\gamma$ this is (d). By [F5] clause (b) applied with $R=J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$, which is positive of trace one by step 1.3, the operator $\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$ is positive of trace one, so its conjugate $\gamma$ is a density operator on $H$. If instead another named slot is retained, the same computation with the corresponding slot operator produces $\gamma'$ with $n\operatorname{tr}((\gamma'-\gamma)O)=0$ for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$, hence $\gamma'=\gamma$ on testing against the rank-one operators $O=T_{u,v}$, for which $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma u,v\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]); this proves (e) as well. [F5, F7, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, algebra]
(a) For every endomorphism $R$ of $V\otimes W$ there is a unique endomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_W R$ of $V$ with
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes I_W)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\operatorname{End}(V),$$

namely $\operatorname{Tr}_WR=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_j\circ R\circ\iota_j$, where $\iota_j(v)=v\otimes f_j$ and $\varphi_j(x\otimes w)=\langle w,f_j\rangle x$; it does not depend on the orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $W$, and the analogous definition gives $\operatorname{Tr}_V R$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_VR)B)=\operatorname{tr}(R(I_V\otimes B))$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_W$ is linear, positive (it maps positive endomorphisms to positive endomorphisms) and trace preserving on density matrices: if $R\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}R=1$ then $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=1$; and $\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*$ for every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$, where $C:W\to V$ is the coefficient map determined by $\Psi=\sum_jCf_j\otimes f_j$.

with $k\le\min(m,n)$, orthonormal families $(v_r)\subseteq V$, $(u_r)\subseteq W$ and $s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_k>0$ uniquely determined by $\Psi$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient map; moreover $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when $k=1$, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; mixed-state separability is not decided by this criterion.
$$\operatorname{Tr}_W\Bigl(\sum_a(I_V\otimes M_a)R(I_V\otimes M_a^*)\Bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_WR .$$

1.1 [Existence and uniqueness of the partial trace] Define $\operatorname{Tr}_WR:=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_jR\iota_j$, a linear endomorphism of $V$. Computed in the basis $(e_i\otimes f_j)$ and using [F2], the matrix of $\varphi_j$ contracts the $W$-index into $f_j$, and the total matrix of $\operatorname{Tr}_WR$ has entries $(\operatorname{Tr}_WR)_{i i'}=\sum_jR_{ij,i'j}$; hence, with $(A)_{i'i''}$ the matrix of $A$, $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A)=\sum_{i,i',j}R_{ij,i'j}A_{i'i}=\operatorname{tr}(R(A\otimes I_W))$. Uniqueness: if $S$ and $S'$ both satisfy the pairing identity, then $\operatorname{tr}((S-S')A)=0$ for all $A$; taking $A=T_{\alpha,\beta}$ (the rank-one endomorphism $v\mapsto\langle v,\beta\rangle\alpha$) for $\alpha,\beta$ ranging over a basis of $V$ and using [F1] and [F2] extracts every matrix entry of $S-S'$, so $S=S'$. Basis independence: the defining identity involves only the basis-independent trace [F2]; equivalently the formula with another orthonormal basis $(g_j)$ yields the same operator by the uniqueness just proved. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Positivity and trace preservation] If $R\ge0$ then for every $x\in V$, $\langle(\operatorname{Tr}_WR)x,x\rangle=\sum_j\langle R(x\otimes f_j),x\otimes f_j\rangle\ge0$ because $R\ge0$ [F4] and each summand is a nonnegative real; hence $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$. Taking $A=I_V$ in the defining identity gives $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=\operatorname{tr}R$; consequently a density matrix $R$ (positive, $\operatorname{tr}R=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]) has $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and trace $1$, so $(\operatorname{Tr}_W)$ maps density matrices to density matrices. [step 1.1, given, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Reduced state of a pure vector] Let $\Psi=\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ and define $C:W\to V$ by $Cf_j=\sum_ic_{ij}e_i$, so that $\Psi=\sum_jCf_j\otimes f_j$ by [F1] (insert the expansions of the $Cf_j$). For the rank-one endomorphism $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ and $A\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, the defining identity of step 1.1 gives $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_WT_{\Psi,\Psi})A)=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\Psi,\Psi}(A\otimes I))=\langle(A\otimes I)\Psi,\Psi\rangle$, and substituting the expansion yields $\sum_{i,i'}\langle A e_i,e_{i'}\rangle\sum_jc_{ij}\overline{c_{i'j}}=\operatorname{tr}(A\,CC^*)$, using the matrix of $CC^*$ in the basis $(e_i)$. Since this holds for all $A$ and the operator is determined by its pairings with all $A$ (step 1.1), $\operatorname{Tr}_WT_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Purity and the product criterion] By steps 2.2 and 3.1, $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_WT_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*$ has eigenvalues $s_r^2$ with multiplicity by [F3], so for $\|\Psi\|=1$ we have $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1=\sum_rs_r^2$. Since all $s_r$ are positive, $\sum_rs_r^4\le(\sum_rs_r^2)^2=1$ with equality exactly when at most one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. $k=1$; and $k=1$ means $\Psi=s_1v_1\otimes u_1$ is a product vector, conversely a product vector has $C$ of rank one by step 2.2. This is the stated criterion; it concerns pure vectors only. [step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Finite nonselective no-signalling] Let $(M_a)$ satisfy $\sum_aM_a^*M_a=I_W$. For $A\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, using the defining identity of step 1.1 and the identity $(I\otimes M_a^*)(A\otimes I)=(A\otimes M_a^*)$ together with cyclicity [F2] inside the finite trace, $\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_W\sum_a(I\otimes M_a)R(I\otimes M_a^*))A\bigr)=\sum_a\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes M_a^*M_a)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes\sum_aM_a^*M_a)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes I)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A\bigr)$; since this holds for every $A$, the uniqueness in step 1.1 gives $\operatorname{Tr}_W(\sum_a(I\otimes M_a)R(I\otimes M_a^*))=\operatorname{Tr}_WR$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra] ∎

findings.problem: Declared model(d)(i),(ii) uses scalar Theta while the declared species space has N copies of the one-particle spin factor; target multiplicity should be (2s+1)^N. The model writes C^(2s+1), whereas its N=2,s=1/2 exchange consumer uses C^4. Source41 scalar sector application does not by itself provide the combined spatial-and-spin permutation transport.

paragraphs:
(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* With $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$
the Euclidean product unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], form the labelled
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clause (b)
whose potential is
$V(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$; by that theorem
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] the
transported projections $\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}$ reduce
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and the restriction
$$H_N^\sigma:=\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)H_{\mathrm{lab}}\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)\big|_{\operatorname{ran}(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1})}$$
is a self-adjoint operator on the transported sector; the model identifies it
with the restriction of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ to
$\Theta^{-1}$-transported $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the tensor reading.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. A more singular declared
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}$, such as $-g/|x|$, is used only through a separate
self-adjointness statement, which the model must supply before the operator is
read as an observable.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* With $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$
the Euclidean product unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], form the labelled
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clause (b)
whose potential is
$V(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$; by that theorem
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] the
transported projections $\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}$ reduce
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and the restriction
$$H_N^\sigma:=\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)H_{\mathrm{lab}}\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)\big|_{\operatorname{ran}(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1})}$$
is a self-adjoint operator on the transported sector; the model identifies it
with the restriction of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ to
$\Theta^{-1}$-transported $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the tensor reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* With the singular data of clause (c)(ii), the
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_V$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clause (b)
is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and
bounded below, and by clause (d) of that theorem its restrictions to the
symmetric and antisymmetric sectors are self-adjoint; the model's sector
energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ is that restriction, with the same reading as in
(i).

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* With $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$
the Euclidean product unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], form the labelled
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clause (b)
whose potential is
$V(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$; by that theorem
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] the
transported projections $\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}$ reduce
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and the restriction
$$H_N^\sigma:=\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)H_{\mathrm{lab}}\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)\big|_{\operatorname{ran}(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1})}$$
is a self-adjoint operator on the transported sector; the model identifies it
with the restriction of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ to
$\Theta^{-1}$-transported $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the tensor reading.

- **Why the sector restriction is legitimate.** In the spatial realizations
  the permutation unitaries preserve the domain $W^{2,2}$ and commute with
  $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, which is exactly the hypothesis of the
  permutation-restricted self-adjointness theorem; in the finite-mode
  realization the bounded operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with the
  $U_\pi$ by construction, and a bounded operator commuting with a projection
  restricts to a self-adjoint operator on its range.
- **Units.** $m$ is in kg, $\hbar$ in J s, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\|V\|_\infty$
  in J, $W$ in J and $\kappa$ in J m; in the finite-mode realization $h$ and
  $W$ are declared directly in joules. No magnetic coupling, spin-orbit term or
  velocity-dependent interaction is part of this model.

[F4] **Sector self-adjointness and domain.** In the bounded case the operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clauses (b), (c)); in the Coulomb case with bounded $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ it is self-adjoint with the same domain ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clauses (b), (c)); the transported antisymmetric projection reduces it, and the restriction $H_2^-$ is self-adjoint on the sector ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] clause (e)).

1.2 [Domain membership and the one-body expectation] Both $u$ and $v$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, so $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ by [F5]; tensoring with the smooth spin vectors and transporting by $\Theta$ and the spin identification places $\Phi_\pm$ in the domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ of [F4]. The one-body operator $h_1+h_2$ with the declared $h$ acts as the identity on the spin factor, so by [F1] the pairing of $h_1+h_2$ with $\varphi_\pm\otimes\chi_\mp$ equals the spatial pairing with $\varphi_\pm$; expanding the two terms of $\varphi_\pm$ and using orthonormality gives $\langle(h_1+h_2)\varphi_\pm,\varphi_\pm\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$ for both signs. [F1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

(e) *application*: let $N\ge1$, $m>0$, $\hbar>0$, let $r\ge1$, let
$V_{\mathrm{ext}},W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and bounded, put
$V(X):=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$ on
$\mathbb R^{3N}$, let $K$ be the free kinetic operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] with all masses
$m_i=m$, let $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$ be
the iterated Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), let $U_\pi$ be the
permutation unitaries of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]
and set
$$U_\pi^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\Theta\,U_\pi\,\Theta^{-1},\qquad P_\pm^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\Theta\,P_\pm^{(N)}\,\Theta^{-1}.$$
Then $H:=K+M_V$ satisfies the hypotheses above for the representation
$U_\pi^{\mathrm{phys}}$, so $P_\pm^{\mathrm{phys}}$ reduce $H$ and the
restrictions of $H$ to the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors are self-adjoint
on those sectors.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N\ge1$, let
$m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ and $\hbar>0$, write points of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ as
$X=(x_1,\dots,x_N)$ with $x_i\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the
Plancherel transform of [[thm-plancherel]] with the convention
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(X)e^{-2\pi iX\cdot\xi}\,dX$ on $L^1$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]). Define the quadratic weight and the
free kinetic operator
$$\kappa(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_N):=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{\hbar^2}{2m_i}|\xi_i|^2,\qquad K:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_\kappa\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(K):=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C):\ \kappa\,\mathcal F_2u\in L^2\}$$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]).
Let $V:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and bounded, with
$\|V\|_\infty:=\operatorname{ess\,sup}|V|<\infty$, and let $M_V$ be
multiplication by $V$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]

and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state

reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
Let a **declared species sector** with one-particle space $H$, mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice

findings.problem: Noninteracting theorem(c) claims 0<Z for every declared sector although(b) permits fermionic N>d and proof3.1 gives the empty sum. The assertion that Z is bounded by configuration count also lacks an energy lower bound of zero: N=d=1, one-particle h=-I, beta=1 gives Z=e>1. This example is inside the declared finite-mode model.

paragraphs:
(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: for every $\beta>0$ the number
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in W(N,d)\\ \lambda_j\le1\ \text{if }\sigma=-}}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is a finite sum with $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$, bounded by the number of
occupation configurations; if $\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$ the ground eigenvalue
is $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and if $\sigma=+$ it is
$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, and for every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
one has $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on
the eigenspace of $E_0$;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: for every $\beta>0$ the number
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in W(N,d)\\ \lambda_j\le1\ \text{if }\sigma=-}}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is a finite sum with $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$, bounded by the number of
occupation configurations; if $\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$ the ground eigenvalue
is $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and if $\sigma=+$ it is
$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, and for every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
one has $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on
the eigenspace of $E_0$;

3.1 [Partition sum and ground energy] The trace of $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is the sum of $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ over the eigenvalues with multiplicity, read on the orthogonal sector bases of step 2.1: $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$ over the occupation configurations of clause (c), a finite nonempty sum of positive numbers for $\sigma=+$ and for $\sigma=-$ with $N\le d$, and empty (no sector states) for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$. If $\sigma=-$, then for every configuration $\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d$ with $\sum\lambda_j=N$ the support $J=\operatorname{supp}\lambda$ has $N$ elements and $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j\ge\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ because the latter is the sum of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues; equality holds exactly for $J$ the set of indices of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues. If $\sigma=+$, then $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\ge\varepsilon_{(1)}\sum_j\lambda_j=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, with equality exactly when every occupied mode has eigenvalue $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally, expanding a unit $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the orthogonal sector basis of step 2.1 gives $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2\lambda_\lambda\ge E_0$ with the stated equality case, where the coefficients are normalized. This proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]
